# Risks

**Medium — it changes the model-facing speaker label on every group turn, and adds one primary-DB transaction to the group hot path.**

The label change is the point of the PR and every pinned assertion moved with it. The new transaction is per group turn, keyed by an advisory lock on the binding, and a registry failure fails the turn closed at `account_resolution` rather than proceeding — deliberate, because a group turn with an unknown speaker would either mis-attribute the message or skip the PII guard, but it is a new dependency on the hot path and worth knowing about.

Direct (non-group) turns are untouched: no roster, no lookup, guard passes through by identity, prompt byte-identical.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

### The defect

The speaker label was `${actor.displayName ?? "Participant"} [participant ${8 hex of sha256(handle)}]`, prefixed into the text the model reads. Blooio (iMessage) sends no display name, so on that connector **every** speaker was literally `Participant [participant 0da02073]`.

Two consequences, both observed live:
1. **The tag leaked into a real group reply**: *"Let's go with Bombay Brasserie. It hits the quiet vibe, has a great vegetarian menu for 0da02073, and is upscale for the weekend."* Note it echoed the **bare digest**, not the bracketed form — a regex stripping `[participant …]` would not have caught it. A high-entropy token is both unsafe to echo and impossible to enumerate, so nothing downstream could recognise or sanitise it.
2. **She could not name anyone**, and mis-attributed: *"Since she has the keys"* about the wrong person.

### The change

A per-binding participant registry (`personal_shared_group_participants`, migration 0311) assigns each speaker a stable 1-based **ordinal** in first-seen order, and stores an optional `display_name`. The label becomes `display_name ?? "Participant <ordinal>"` — stable for the life of the binding, human-safe if echoed, and **enumerable**, which is what finally makes a guard possible.

- **Ordinal assignment is atomic.** One transaction takes `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(bindingId), …)` — the repo's existing two-int4 form — then a single `INSERT … SELECT COALESCE(MAX(ordinal),0)+1 … ON CONFLICT (binding_id, platform_user_id) DO UPDATE SET last_seen_at = now() RETURNING …`, then reads the roster inside the same transaction. `UNIQUE (binding_id, ordinal)` is the backstop, not the mechanism. Proven, not asserted: a real-PostgreSQL test runs 12 concurrent first-time speakers; with the advisory lock removed 3 of its 4 cases fail on the unique index (PGlite serialises transactions and cannot establish the interleaving, which is why that file targets real PG).
- **Names come from the connector where one exists.** Telegram and Discord do send a sender name, so `display_name` is populated from it and those groups render real names — better than before, where the name was there but wrapped around a hex tag. Blooio still renders `Participant N`.
- **A display name is attacker-controlled, so it is sanitised before it can become a label.** Invisible characters (`\p{Cc}`, `\p{Zl}`, `\p{Zp}`, and the bidi controls `U+200E/200F`, `U+202A–202E`, `U+2066–2069`) collapse to spaces; whitespace collapses; over 128 characters is rejected rather than truncated (truncation can split a grapheme cluster, and the ordinal fallback is always safe). A **colon is rejected outright**: the delivery text is `${label}: ${message}` on one line, so `Ada: sure, go ahead` would stage a second speaker turn inside this speaker's own. A name that matches the generated label shape or the owner label is rejected, reusing `isGroupParticipantLabel` and an exported owner-label constant rather than a second matcher. And a name containing **any participant's connector handle** is rejected — otherwise a member could set their Telegram name to another member's phone number and put it straight into the prompt, undoing the registry's whole privacy property; that check shares one definition of "a handle occurrence" with the egress guard.
- **Collisions: first claimant keeps the name**, the loser falls back to their own ordinal. This is the impersonation defence rather than a tiebreak — a member who renames to an existing member's name becomes their own ordinal, not a second copy of that person. Resolution runs inside the same advisory-locked transaction, proven with three backends claiming one name at once.
- **Egress guard.** On group replies only (both the dedicated-bridge and shared-runtime return sites), any raw connector handle of a participant in this binding is replaced with that participant's label. Exact-substring plus digits-only core, boundary-guarded, longest-variant-first, floored at 6 characters so a degenerate handle cannot corrupt ordinary prose.
- **Prompt.** One line is appended to a *copy* of the character system prompt when the channel type is GROUP, in the cloud shared-runtime seam. `packages/core` is deliberately untouched: #25279 changed core's Stage-1 prompt and #25341 had to repair the regression that caused, so a change there needs a much wider evidence bar than this PR carries.

`display_name` was originally specified to ship unpopulated; that was wrong, because dropping `actor.displayName` from the label would have regressed Telegram, where real names are already available. The mutation check for it is explicit below.

# Risks

**Low–medium.** The receipt is additive: it attaches a new `data.workspace_delta` key and never changes SHELL's exit status, stdout/stderr, or control flow. Every failure path degrades to an explicit `indeterminate` receipt rather than throwing out of the handler.

The one behavioural change is in `planner-loop`: the coding-completion gate now also treats a receipt-attested workspace change as mutation evidence, and requires the clearing verification to itself report `unchanged`. A verifier command that mutates the workspace no longer clears the gate. Receipt-less and `indeterminate` results keep the previous legacy behaviour, so environments without receipts are unaffected.

Per-call cost: two local `git status` fingerprints per foreground SHELL run. Probes are capped at 10s and 64MB and are excluded from the reported command duration.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Foreground SHELL executions could mutate the workspace with nothing in the result attesting that they had. Shell-driven mutations that carry no WRITE/EDIT step — code generation, `git apply`, deletes, formatters — were invisible to the runtime's mutation-verification gate.

This adds a typed, content-free `WorkspaceDeltaReceipt`:

- **`packages/core/src/types/workspace-delta.ts`** — the receipt type, canonical `WORKSPACE_DELTA_RECEIPT_KEY` (`workspace_delta`), version constant, and a validating parser/reader.
- **`plugins/plugin-coding-tools/src/lib/workspace-delta.ts`** — local Git worktree fingerprinting. Captures HEAD, `git status --porcelain=v2`, and the byte contents of worktree-dirty tracked plus non-ignored untracked files (the one dimension status cannot distinguish when a file is dirty both before and after). Reduces the before/after pair to `changed` / `unchanged` / `indeterminate`.
- **`plugins/plugin-coding-tools/src/actions/bash.ts`** — attaches the receipt on every foreground path: success, nonzero exit, timeout, output-limit, and dispatch error.
- **`packages/core/src/runtime/planner-loop.ts`** — the coding-completion gate consumes the receipt.

Design constraints held throughout:

- **Content-free.** No file names, contents, or diffs — only fingerprints and a typed status.
- **Never throws.** Every capture failure becomes an explicit `indeterminate` reason (`not_a_git_worktree`, `git_unavailable`, `baseline_capture_failed`, `post_capture_failed`, `execution_route_unknown`).
- **Strictly local and read-only.** Git runs with `--no-optional-locks`, never through the capability router. `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE` and object-directory overrides are stripped so the probe always describes the cwd's worktree.
- **Honest about what it cannot attest.** Remotely routed capability-router execution carries no local receipt at all; a dispatch failure with a router present reports `execution_route_unknown`.
- **Failure and mutation are independent.** A nonzero exit or a timed-out command can still have written files, and still reports `changed`.

Background sessions are out of scope for this PR.

## Review fix: the parser is a trust boundary (@ss251)

The first revision validated the *shape* of a receipt but not whether its
fields supported the status it declared. `parseWorkspaceDeltaReceipt` accepted
`{version: 1, status: "unchanged"}` with no fingerprints at all, `unchanged`
with two different digests, `changed` with identical digests, and
`indeterminate` with no reason. Because the gate clears pending mutation
evidence on `receipt.status === "unchanged"`, any alternate or malformed
`ActionResult` supplying the bare shape cleared the completion gate without
establishing a before/after relationship. A wrong value, not a thrown error, so
no outer boundary contained it. Confirmed against the exact reviewed head
before changing anything.

**Invariant now enforced — the receipt's own fields must prove its status:**

| status | requires |
| --- | --- |
| `unchanged` | both digests, no reason, `before === after` |
| `changed` | both digests, no reason, `before !== after` |
| `indeterminate` | a typed reason, never an `afterFingerprint`, and only the `beforeFingerprint` its particular capture failure could have produced |

The per-reason fingerprint rule matches what the producer emits: a baseline
that never completed cannot have produced a digest (`not_a_git_worktree`,
`baseline_capture_failed`, `execution_route_unknown` forbid one), a
post-execution failure always has the baseline in hand (`post_capture_failed`
requires one), and `git_unavailable` is the one reason legitimately either,
because git can disappear before the baseline or between the two captures.

A second commit closes a fail-open path found while probing the fix: field
reads went through the prototype chain, so an inherited digest pair satisfied
requirements a bare receipt could not meet on its own, and a polluted
`Object.prototype` would have turned a rejected receipt into an accepted one.
Reads are now own-property only.

Both fixes are contained in the parser. No producer, SHELL, planner
architecture, or remote-execution behaviour changed.

**Environment note for anyone reproducing locally.** This branch was developed in a checkout under `/root`. This is a property of the checkout location, not of the change:

```
checkout under /root       branch: 5 failed | 154 passed (159)
checkout under /tmp        branch: 159 passed (159)
checkout under /tmp        merge-base (8b4fff7e): 152 passed (152)
```

159 - 152 = exactly the 7 receipt cases this PR adds; no pre-existing test changes status. Reproduce from any path outside `/root`.

Very large or pathological worktrees will resolve to `indeterminate` rather than slowing the turn.

# Risks

Medium. This changes Settings route composition, account-session gating, and
tenant-sensitive Organization query keys on desktop and narrow layouts. It does
not change cloud APIs, billing calculations, persistence, infrastructure, or
backend behavior. Account bodies unmount synchronously at sign-out start,

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Mounts Billing, API Keys, Sessions & privacy, and Organization as explicit
  account-footer destinations in cloud-only Settings instead of silently
  falling back to General.
- Keeps those entries out of the normal groups and exposes them through the
  same account menu on wide and narrow layouts, preserving canonical hashes,
  active state, narrow back navigation, and header actions.
- Reactively gates the destinations on either a connected cloud session or a
  restored management credential, including same-document token changes.
- Suppresses every prior account history entry as soon as sign-out starts, so
  Back cannot remount account data while disconnect is pending or has failed;
  a still-observed session gets a persistent, explicit retry affordance.
- Mounts the registered `cloud/invoices/:id` route inside the Settings fallback
  router, making invoice “View” and “Back to Billing” functional.
- Partitions all Organization reads by authenticated user and preserves RBAC
  gates, preventing stale tenant data from appearing after an account switch.
- Bridges only lifted Cloud text utilities to AA-readable Eliza colors without
  mutating the NuPhy fill, border, or ring tokens.
- Uses the globally defined opaque surface token for Organization invite,
  member, credential, revoke, and Select portals rendered outside
  `.nuphy-scope`.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue).

2a:T1f16,## What

Fixes the multi-agent "endless hell loop" in group channels with a layered design: two advisory providers (soft signal, graceful behavior for capable models) plus a deterministic decision-path gate (hard floor that works identically regardless of model size). Direct ask from Shaw + Shadow in #cc-eliza (2026-08-23): revive/modernize the old ANXIETY provider for group chat, add bot-awareness so agents don't loop with each other, and make the anti-loop guarantee hold for small models (gemma-class) that don't reliably follow prompt guidance.

## The three pieces

### 1. `ANXIETY` provider (soft, group-only)

`packages/core/src/features/basic-capabilities/providers/anxiety.ts`

Shaw's original anxiety provider picked 3 RANDOM canned "you are too verbose" strings per channel type — static, evidence-free. This reimplementation computes pressure from LIVE room state:

- **Talked-too-much:** the agent's share of the recent dialogue window vs its fair share of the floor (`1 / (participants + 1)`). Room-aware by construction: the same agent turn count produces more pressure in a crowded room, and a crowd factor ramps busier rooms faster ("anxiety based on room").
- **Ping-pong:** a strict tail alternation between the agent and ONE other sender (A→B→A→B) adds pressure even at moderate overall share.
- **Dampeners:** zero pressure when the agent has been quiet; strong damping when a human just directly addressed the agent — genuine engagement is never suppressed.

Output is dynamic guidance text that scales with computed pressure — light "keep it short" at low pressure, "you have sent 8 of the last 12 messages, others should have the floor, prefer IGNORE / a reaction / silence" at high pressure. IGNORE-as-valid-response framing kept from the original. Calibration is an exported constant passed by parameter, so hosts can add per-room calibration later without changing the provider contract; no agent-specific hardcoding.

**Group-only:** GROUP / VOICE_GROUP / THREAD / WORLD / FORUM. DMs return the empty result — asserted bidirectionally in tests (same history that fires in a group is inert in a DM, both via explicit `content.channelType` and via room-row type resolution).

### 2. `BOT_AWARENESS` provider (soft, group-only, separate per Shaw's framing)

`packages/core/src/features/basic-capabilities/providers/botAwareness.ts`

Explicit "you are talking to another bot" awareness. Bot detection uses the connector-stamped `fromBot` metadata — the same ground truth the transcript formatter renders as `Name (bot)` and the bot-noise triage gate reads. Never name-guessing. Fires only when the latest inbound turn is bot-authored AND there has been bot↔agent back-and-forth with NO intervening human turn; escalates from "don't mirror its conversational reflexes" to "this exchange is N messages deep with no human — let it drop" as the human-free exchange deepens. Renders nothing when a human is active, so it degrades to normal behavior.

### 3. Deterministic bot-loop gate (hard floor, model-size independent)

`packages/core/src/services/message/bot-loop-gate.ts`, wired into `MessageService` immediately after the bot-noise triage.

**Why code, not prompt:** the loop is worst on agents running small models (remilio on gemma-4), and small models do not reliably follow soft prompt guidance — a purely advisory fix would be ignored by exactly the agent most likely to cause the loop. This gate trips BEFORE any model call, so it behaves identically on gemma-4 and frontier models: the model never gets the chance to loop.

Trip condition (all must hold; anything unverifiable fails OPEN):
- inbound message is positively bot-authored (`fromBot`),
- multi-party channel (group-only, same scoping as the providers),
- the agent has already produced ≥ N consecutive turns since the last human message in the room (default N=2, `ELIZA_BOT_LOOP_MAX_AGENT_TURNS`, clamped ≥1 so the agent can always answer a bot once — the loop starts at the reply-to-a-reply).

When tripped: deterministic IGNORE, run terminalized with status `bot_loop_gate`, zero model calls. A human speaking resets the counters naturally, so human conversation is never suppressed. **Strictly additive:** all existing gates (mute, personality reply-gate, bot-noise triage) run unchanged; this only ever biases toward silence, never speech. Opt-out: `ELIZA_BOT_LOOP_GATE=0`.

## Layering with existing work

- **#25405 (register-aware + restraint defaults):** added IGNORE-biased multi-agent rules to the shouldRespond prompts ("never reply to another bot's reply", "one speaker per human message") in both `packages/prompts` and the cloud-bootstrap planner template. Those prompt rules are the soft layer for models that read; the bot-loop gate here is the hard floor beneath them for models that don't. Same policy, two enforcement strengths — the gate does not duplicate the prompt text and cannot fight it (both bias the same direction).
- **#25283 / successor #25356 (engagement gate, classifyLeadingVocative, agent-name-match):** those decide ADDRESSING (is this message for me). These providers compose advisory STATE (how much have I been talking, is my interlocutor a bot). Orthogonal by design: the providers' human-addressed dampener reads platform mention/reply + whole-word name match (a deliberately lightweight mirror — providers can't import services/message without a cycle), and never gates a response. Since #25283 closed superseded by draft #25356, nothing here reuses its unmerged utils; if #25356 lands, its addressing classifier can replace the dampener's name check in a follow-up.

## Hot-path cost

No model calls, no embeddings, no new DB query shapes. Providers read the composed `RECENT_MESSAGES` state on turn recompose (asserted: zero adapter scans); on first compose and in the gate, the fallback room-scan uses exactly the newest-first shape the runtime's turn-scoped single-flight memo coalesces (`coalesceRoomMessagesScan`), sharing the superset fetch RECENT_MESSAGES/FACTS/ATTACHMENTS already issue. `BOT_AWARENESS` short-circuits before any window load when the inbound turn isn't bot-authored.

## Proof

`anxiety.test.ts` (15) + `bot-loop-gate.test.ts` (8), all deterministic (real `AgentRuntime` + `InMemoryDatabaseAdapter`, throwing `useModel` stub in the gate tests proves zero model involvement):

- anxiety rises with agent-turn dominance (high-watermark text + pressure value asserted)
- anxiety ramps on sustained single-participant ping-pong
- anxiety stays silent when the agent has been quiet
- anxiety damped (not silenced) when a human addresses the agent by name
- anxiety INERT in DMs bidirectionally: same max-pressure history fires in GROUP, returns `{text:"",values:{},data:{}}` in DM via both channelType paths
- room-awareness: identical agent activity → more pressure with more participants (pure-function proof)
- recompose path: composed state consumed with zero adapter scans
- bot-awareness fires on bot interlocutor + no intervening human; escalates at depth ≥4; quiet when a human spoke in the gap; quiet for human interlocutors; inert in DMs
- **gate: deterministic IGNORE for an all-bot back-and-forth with no human turn — with `useModel` stubbed to throw, proving the verdict cannot depend on model instruction-following (the gemma-4 coverage proof)**
- gate does NOT trip when a human has spoken since the agent's last turn
- gate allows the first reply to a bot; fails open for human/untagged senders, unknown channels, DB read failure; honors opt-out + threshold clamping/raising

No-regression: recentMessages, channelTopics, userEmotionSignal, provider-descriptions, bot-noise-triage, compose-state-provider-purity, message-runtime-stage1 (180), message-stage1-prompt-tier — all green (the one turn-read-coalescing failure is pre-existing on develop, verified by stashing this change). `tsc --noEmit` clean, Biome clean on touched files.

## Outcome

Personal WhatsApp now stores Baileys credentials and Signal keys in one connector-owned per-account snapshot under the canonical elizaOS state directory. The hard cut removes Baileys multi-file auth authority and rejects broad/operator directories, foreign files, symlinks, hard links, account collisions, corruption, partial writes, and stale state handles.

The commit protocol durably records pending and confirmed snapshot hashes. Known pre-snapshot failure restores the prior confirmed hash before the live generation can continue. Any ambiguous or post-snapshot failure retires that generation and requires restart readback; logout independently proves directory ownership before local deletion and can recover an owned corrupt snapshot without deleting foreign content. Status is strictly read-only.

Baileys is pinned exactly at `7.0.0-rc14` in the manifest and lockfile and remains bundled in-process; no external bridge application or daemon is introduced.

2e:T3451,> **Draft status:** based on `ed4d4a3`; will rebase before ready. Part of `nubs/demo-night`. Heads-up @lalalune: may overlap your openviking attachment-awareness track — happy to fold this into it.


### What

Inbound Blooio (iMessage/SMS) image attachments currently reach the personal
Shared turn as the literal `[media: <url>]` text the gateway adapter
synthesizes, so the model never sees the image. This PR adds an additive,
flag-gated enrichment path: with `ELIZA_APP_INBOUND_MEDIA_VISION="true"` on the
Worker, the route fetches the allowlisted Blooio media, describes it with a
vision model, and delivers the turn as:

```
[media: <url>]

[Attached image description]
<vision description>
```

With the flag off (the default), a missing vision provider key, or any
enrichment failure, the delivered message is byte-identical to today's
`[media: url]` text and the user's turn is never dropped.

### Why

The shared turn's default text model cannot see images (only the Node/dedicated
runtime path has `ModelType.IMAGE_DESCRIPTION` via plugin-elizacloud). This
follows the existing Telegram voice-note precedent exactly: the gateway
resolves media context, posts it as a structured field, and the route enriches
`deliveryMessage` before the turn — no changes to `run-shared-agent-turn`.

### How

- **Gateway** (`packages/cloud/services/gateway-webhook/src/webhook-handler.ts`):
  for Blooio one-to-one turns, forwards the adapter's already-allowlisted
  `event.mediaUrls` on the personal-Shared POST body and raises the request
  timeout to 90s for media turns (mirroring the voice ceiling) so a vision
  enrichment cannot be aborted mid-flight and re-run. Media turns adopt the
  voice-note retry posture: attempts capped at 2 (stale-auth inline retry
  only) with status/transport re-POSTs disabled, because an aborted long turn
  may still be running server-side and a re-POST would overlap it and re-run
  the vision call. Blooio group events (which carry `mediaUrls` but are never
  forwarded as media and run no vision) keep the plain text-turn 30s
  timeout and full retry budget.
- **Allowlist one-source-of-truth**
  (`packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/eliza-app/blooio-media-allowlist.ts`):
  canonical https + Blooio-domain predicate, dependency-free so the gateway
  test can import it. The adapter keeps its runtime-local copy (the gateway
  must not depend on cloud-shared at runtime); a parity test pins the two
  byte-identical, following the existing `billing.test.ts` precedent.
- **Helper**
  (`packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/eliza-app/describe-inbound-media.ts`):
  `describeInboundImageMedia(env, urls)` — fail-closed typed
  `InboundMediaVisionDisabledError` when the flag is off or no provider key is
  configured; SSRF-guarded byte fetch via `safeFetch` with `redirect: "error"`
  (redirect hops are only SSRF-checked, not allowlist-checked, so any redirect
  fails the fetch rather than letting an open redirect on an allowlisted host
  reach an arbitrary origin), an `image/*`
  content-type gate and an 8 MiB streamed size cap (Content-Length is treated
  as untrusted); concurrent fetches settle via `Promise.allSettled` so a
  failing sibling cannot leave in-flight bodies buffering in the isolate;
  `generateText` with `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` image parts, bounded
  output tokens, 45s abort. Every per-turn failure (fetch, non-image,
  oversize, provider error, empty completion, length-truncated completion) is
  a typed `InboundMediaDescriptionError` with a machine-readable `reason`.
  Empty/truncated completions are rejected, never delivered, per the
  repository prompt-integrity rule.
- **Route**
  (`packages/cloud/api/internal/eliza-app/personal-shared/messages/route.ts`):
  additive optional `mediaUrls` (1–4, allowlist-re-validated, Blooio-only) on
  the twilio/blooio schema variant; a `media_description` delivery stage;
  disabled → debug log + raw text, typed description failure → `logger.error`
  (reported, since the turn still succeeds) + raw text, unexpected errors
  propagate to the J1 boundary and fail the delivery with the
  `media_description` failure-stage header.
- **Bindings**: `ELIZA_APP_INBOUND_MEDIA_VISION?: string` documented in
  `packages/cloud/shared/src/types/cloud-worker-env.ts`.

### Flag rollout

1. Ships dark: no Worker/wrangler config change, so the flag is unset and the
   behavior is byte-identical everywhere (only the gateway body gains the
   ignored-by-default `mediaUrls` field).
2. Enable on staging (`ELIZA_APP_INBOUND_MEDIA_VISION=true` as a Worker var)
   and send a real inbound iMessage image to verify the one unproven
   assumption live: that Blooio media URLs are fetchable by the Worker without
   provider auth **and without redirects** (the fetch now rejects any redirect
   hop; if Blooio legitimately serves media via a CDN redirect, widen this
   deliberately with a per-hop allowlist re-check rather than reverting to
   follow-mode). If they need auth, fall back to a gateway-side byte fetch
   (Node `safeFetch` with true socket pinning) posting a size-capped base64
   `imageAttachment` field, exactly like `voiceNote`.
3. Production enablement after staging evidence **and** an abuse-spend gate:
   the `media_description` stage spends unmetered pooled-key vision credit and
   is reachable by any inbound sender to the connected number (unlike the
   voice path, which requires a linked account), so a per-sender or
   per-connector rate limit — or routing the describe call through the org
   billing meter — must land before the flag is set in production. Follow-up
   issue to be filed with this PR. Disabling the flag restores current
   behavior instantly, no deploy of the gateway required.

## Review

An internal fix-first review of the initial revision found five issues; all
are addressed in the current revision:

1. **(major, fixed)** `describe-inbound-media.ts`: the media fetch used
   safeFetch's default redirect-follow mode. Redirect hops are re-validated
   only against the SSRF/private-IP guard — not the Blooio allowlist — so an
   open redirect on any allowlisted host (api.blooio.com is a general API
   host) could have fetched attacker-chosen bytes from any public origin and
   fed them to the vision model, contradicting the module's own safety claim.
   Fixed by passing `redirect: "error"`: any redirect now fails the fetch as
   `media_fetch_failed`. A regression test pins the init on every call. If
   staging shows Blooio media legitimately redirecting to a CDN, the widening
   must be a deliberate per-hop allowlist re-check (rollout step 2).
2. **(major, fixed)** `webhook-handler.ts`: media turns got the 90s ceiling
   but kept `maxAttempts=3` with status/transport retries enabled — the exact
   combination the voice path avoids. A >90s or 5xx media turn would be
   re-POSTed while the first route execution (fetch + unbilled vision + model
   turn) may still be running server-side, duplicating spend and risking
   overlapping agent turns. Fixed by treating media turns exactly like voice:
   `maxAttempts=2`, `retryStatuses`/`retryTransport` disabled, stale-auth
   inline retry kept. Regression tests pin both the no-retry media posture
   and a retrying text-turn control.
3. **(minor, fixed)** `webhook-handler.ts`: the 90s media-timeout condition
   did not exclude group events, which carry `mediaUrls` but are never
   forwarded as media (no vision runs) — a group image message would hold the
   background slot up to 90s for a plain text turn. Fixed with a single
   `isMediaTurn` predicate (`blooio && !isGroup && mediaUrls`) used by the
   timeout, the retry posture, and the body forward guard; a regression test
   pins the group posture.
4. **(minor, addressed as a rollout gate)** route `media_description` stage:
   once the flag is on, any inbound sender can trigger unmetered pooled-key
   vision spend with no rate limit or billing gate. A production-blocking
   gate is now recorded in rollout step 3 and as an in-code comment at the
   stage; the rate-limit/billing implementation is a follow-up issue, filed
   with this PR, that must land before production enablement.
5. **(minor, fixed)** `describe-inbound-media.ts`: `Promise.all` over the
   concurrent fetches rejected on the first failure while sibling responses
   kept buffering in the isolate until GC. Fixed with `Promise.allSettled`
   (every fetch fully reads its capped body or cancels it) before rethrowing
   the first failure unchanged; a mixed-outcome regression test pins it.

## Limitations (honest)

- **No live verification yet.** The repo evidence policy requires exercising
  the real boundary; the one unverified assumption is whether Blooio media
  URLs are publicly fetchable (the adapter documents no auth contract). This
  must be proven with one real inbound iMessage image on staging before
  production enablement; the `voiceNote`-style gateway byte-fetch fallback is
  the designed escape hatch if they need auth.
- **Billing bypass.** The describe call uses the pooled provider key and
  bypasses per-org billing — the same posture as the existing Whisper voice
  path in this route, but with a wider blast radius: any stranger who texts
  the connected number can trigger the spend, with no linked-account
  requirement. Acceptable while flag-off/staging-only; a per-sender or
  per-connector rate limit (or billing-meter routing) is a hard gate on
  production enablement (rollout step 3).
- **workerd SSRF residual.** `safeFetch` cannot pin sockets on Cloudflare
  Workers (documented in `safe-fetch.ts`); the allowlist restricts targets to
  Blooio-owned domains, but the platform-level DNS-rebinding TOCTOU noted in
  #12229 M5 applies until the Cloudflare egress policy closes it.
- **One-to-one Blooio only.** Group Blooio media and Telegram/Twilio/WhatsApp
  media are out of scope; those turns keep their current behavior.
- **Non-image media** (video, PDF, audio attachments on Blooio) intentionally
  degrade to the raw `[media: url]` text via the `unsupported_media_type`
  path — no attempt is made to describe them.
- **Latency.** An enriched turn adds up to ~15s fetch + ~45s vision on top of
  the model turn; the gateway timeout for media turns was raised to 90s to
  cover it. Blooio webhook-retry interplay past 90s is unchanged from the
  voice path's posture.
- **Pre-existing worktree failures (not from this change):**
  `packages/cloud/api/v1/voice/session/__tests__/ws-lifecycle.test.ts` fails
  `tsc --noEmit`, and two `onboarding-chat.test.ts` cases fail; both reproduce
  on the clean base tree.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Covers the exported Worker-safe helpers, throwing runtime stand-ins, and registries in `elizaos-core.ts`:

- Document-augmentation envelope detection and strip-for-persistence (same-reference no-ops, `<user_request>` extract, language-suffix drop).
- `unwrapUserMessageText` resolution order: retained `userPayloadText`, then stamped wrapped-envelope parse, then raw text; envelope-looking candidates resolve to `""`. Invisible-character and confusable-glyph folding match the skeleton the stub actually builds (ZWSP only keeps the needle when `_` remains).
- `ElizaError` / `isElizaError` / `toElizaError` (same-instance, Error wrap, string/other stringify).
- Settings, env aliases (first partner wins; self-alias skipped), `~` path expansion, truthy env strings, UUID helpers, and owner-entity derivation. `resolveOwnerEntityIdOrDefault` uses the **first** configured owner; a later UUID in contacts does **not** win when the first candidate is not a UUID.
- SSRF guard: private/localhost/internal blocks, public IPv4 literals skip DNS, DNS fail-closed (error / empty / mixed private), 301 POST→GET rewrite, `maxRedirects: 0`. Malformed `http://256.1.1.1/x` throws `TypeError` from `new URL` before SSRF checks.
- Connector registry: empty/missing sources, builtin alias collapse, later-owner field wins, missing-owner unregister is a no-op. Unknown canonicals return the empty-fields merged object (not `null`) because discord is registered at module init.
- Sensitive-request policy branches, metadata redaction, request/response body caps, prompt helpers, Service/Semaphore/BM25 throw vs no-op, `truncateWellFormed` surrogate-safe cut, HTML script/style strip.
- Re-exports (`detectPii`, redaction, `normalizeConnectedAccount`) are driven as real functions. `normalizeConnectedAccount({})` throws core's `ElizaError`, which is **not** `instanceof` the stub's same-named class.

The suite drives the real module. No mocks of the stub.

## What kind of change is this?

Improvements (test coverage only; no production behaviour change).

## Why are we doing this?

The stub is the workerd alias for `@elizaos/core`. It had no colocated test. Coverage records what the code does so a later production edit cannot silently change Worker-safe helpers, throw contracts, or registry merge order.

## What

Adds a new deterministic unit suite for the trust scoring core,
`packages/core/src/features/trust/services/TrustEngine.ts`, which previously had
no test coverage at its own path (the pre-existing
`TrustEngine.confidence.test.ts` is untouched; this diff is a single new file,
+N/-0).

The suite drives the **real** `TrustEngine` through its public API against a
minimal in-memory runtime and a Drizzle-shaped database stub — no module mocks.
All time-dependent behavior (evidence decay, recency windows, hourly rate
limits, the five-minute profile cache) is exercised under frozen fake timers.

## Coverage

- **Lifecycle**: `serviceType`, static `start()` returning a usable engine, and
  `stop()` clearing the profile cache so the next call recomputes.
- **Constructor configuration**: lowered `minimumEvidenceCount` flipping a zero
  confidence to 0.64, full `dimensionWeights` replacement (shallow, not merged),
  `recencyBias: 0` flattening age decay to the 0.5 floor weight, and
  `verificationMultiplier: 1` making verified/unverified evidence equivalent.
- **Dimension arithmetic**: verified/unverified impact mapping with decay and
  verification factors (69.125/62.75 expectations), clamping at both 0 and 100,
  neutral evidence counting toward volume without moving dimensions, and
  context-specific weights (`financial` → 60, unknown action falling back to
  the default 58, `moderation` → 56).
- **Confidence**: minimal-unanimous 0.66, strict seven-day recency boundary
  (evidence exactly at the cutoff is excluded) → 0.56, balanced contradictory
  evidence zeroing consistency → 0.38, and the twenty-item count cap → 1.
- **Evidence loading**: world/room pinning filters, inclusive time-window
  boundaries, DB merge deduplicated on timestamp+type, `Date`-to-ms row
  conversion, malformed stored components/rows raising typed
  `INVALID_STORED_TRUST_EVIDENCE` errors, and DB failures reported through
  `runtime.reportError("TrustEngine.loadEvidence", …)` before rethrowing.
- **Trend analysis**: stable/increasing/decreasing directions computed from the
  oldest stored score, sub-half-point drift rounding to a stable 0.4 rate, the
  one-minute timespan floor producing a 1440 points/day rate instead of a
  division by zero, `lastChangeAt` preservation when unchanged vs stamped when
  changed, evaluator-scoped history filtering, and typed
  `INVALID_STORED_TRUST_PROFILE` rejection of malformed stored profiles.
- **Persistence**: deterministic component ids, default `trust-world` /
  `trust-global` placement, explicit world/room propagation, and update-in-place
  preserving the original `createdAt`.
- **Caching**: identical object served within five minutes, recompute at exactly
  five minutes stale, per-evaluator keying, and FIFO eviction past 2000 entries
  (evicted key recomputes; recent key stays cached).
- **Interaction recording**: diminishing returns weights 1 / 0.75 / 0.5 / 0.25,
  ten-per-entity-per-hour acceptance with silent drop of the eleventh, window
  closed at exactly one hour but reset strictly after, per-entity independence,
  agent-id/description/context fallbacks on persist, scoped per-entity cache
  invalidation, the newest-500 in-memory retention cap, and persistence failures
  reported via `runtime.reportError("TrustEngine.persistEvidence", …)` then
  rethrown.
- **Decisions & convenience APIs**: denial reasons and branch-specific
  suggestions for overall/dimension/interaction/confidence failures, exact-
  equality passes with falsy zero minima, failure precedence order, `evaluateTrust`
  context merging including the observed spread behavior where a partial
  context's `evaluatorId` wins over the parameter, and `getRecentInteractions`
  source/target matching with custom/zero/negative `daysBack` and a strict
  greater-than cutoff.

# Risks

Low. The change narrows an over-eager task (re)creation predicate in a single reconcile function (`reconcileEvent` in `plugins/plugin-calendar/src/meetings/auto-join.ts`). It only *prevents* recreation of one-shot tasks that already ran; it does not alter the first-time scheduling path, the anchor-registration path, the policy-change dismiss/recreate path, or the deletion/ended-event dismiss path (all still covered by the pre-existing suite, which stays green).

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Fixes a lost-idempotency / double-fire bug in calendar meeting auto-join.

`reconcileEvent` decided whether an event's approval/join task already existed by inspecting **only LIVE tasks** (`scheduled | fired | acknowledged`). Once a one-shot task reached a terminal state (`completed | skipped | expired | failed`) it was treated as absent and recreated on the next periodic calendar feed sync — repeatedly, within the same event window:

- **ask policy:** after the owner approves (approval → `completed`, gated join fires), the next sync schedules a **new** approval task, re-prompting the owner to approve a meeting they already approved — once per sync until the event ends.
- **all policy:** after the join task completes (agent already joined), a mid-meeting sync schedules a **new** join anchored at `start − 1min`, which is now in the past → due immediately → the agent **re-joins** the same meeting.

The fix gates (re)creation on `existingForMode` — tasks for this event under the current policy mode in **any non-dismissed** state, not just live ones — so a terminal one-shot task is not resurrected within its window. The `live`/`stale` set still drives the policy-change dismiss/recreate path, and only `dismissed` (the state reserved for tasks we intentionally retired: policy change, deletion, ended event) counts as absent, so a genuine later policy switch can still recreate under the new mode.

```diff
-  const current = live.filter((task) => taskMode(task) === policy);
+  const existingForMode = existing.filter(
+    (task) => taskMode(task) === policy && task.state.status !== "dismissed",
+  );
   // ...find approval/join in existingForMode (not `current`) before scheduling
```

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue).

# Documentation changes needed?

No. Behavior is corrected to match the module's documented contract ("keeps exactly one join task per event"); no public API, schema, or setting changes.

- **regression:** a completed `all` join must still yield to a genuine `all→ask` policy change (asserts the terminal-status gate does not defeat dismiss/recreate — the ask approval+join pair is created).

- Exported deadlines (`MCP_PROVIDER_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` = 10s,

  forward/serve

  `MCP_<SLUG>_STREAMABLE_HTTP_URL`, DoorDash 120s deadline vs other providers
  `timeoutMs: undefined`, builtin-with-override forwards instead of serving

- JSON-RPC parse error, invalid request, id coercion (string/number/null kept;
  other shapes → null)

## What

Adds a new unit suite, `packages/core/src/features/working-memory/readAttachmentAction.test.ts`, covering the ATTACHMENT action's core runtime surface. **Test-only change: one new file, +1106/−0; no production code is touched and no behavior changes.**

## Why

The module's exported surface (`completeAttachmentContent`, `readAttachmentActionKind`, `readAttachmentAction.validate`, `readAttachmentAction.handler`) had aspect-specific suites (`delivery`, `document-world`, `i18n`, `transcription`) but no core suite pinning the shared fundamentals this file locks in:

- kind routing and alias precedence (`action` > `subaction` > `op`; normalization of case/whitespace/hyphens; safe default to `read`; an unrecognized higher-priority field blocks lower aliases rather than falling through)
- validate gating (explicit `attachmentId`/`id`/inline attachments vs. conversation-derived availability) and rejection propagation from history lookup
- record-selection fallbacks: unavailable explicit id (`ATTACHMENT_UNAVAILABLE_OR_UNAUTHORIZED`), empty-window reply, selection menu over multiple history attachments, and multi-record `ATTACHMENT_READ_SELECTION_REQUIRED` with readable byte counts
- byte-exact UTF-8 paging: complete vs. `partial-recoverable` slices, lossless multi-page reassembly of multibyte content, revision-gated continuation, stale-revision and missing-revision failures, invalid offset/limit structured failures (including offsets that would split a code point)
- task-clipboard outcomes driven through the real persistence service in a temp dir: not requested, added, replaced, and skipped-with-reason, plus `suppressActionResultClipboard`
- missing-readable-content messaging (singular/plural, image, transcript-pending, anchored transcription-unavailable honesty)
- save_as_document: verified failure paths (`DOCUMENTS_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`), world resolution via message → room → agent fallback, room-lookup refusal codes, scope validation defaults, complete-content persistence with byte-size metadata
- boundary policy: one `reportError`, generic callback text, and a structured failed result for lookup/model exceptions

The harness is deterministic: a hand-rolled runtime stub drives the real module with scripted model responses — no module mocks, no network, no live model (same style as the sibling `readAttachmentAction.delivery.test.ts`).

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Adds `personal-eliza-group-lifecycle.spec.ts`: the full Personal Shared group-chat lifecycle against the real local Worker, PGlite database and Durable Objects, deterministic and offline. A scripted model server replays the exact HANDLE_RESPONSE / REMINDERS tool-call protocol the shared runtime speaks (so every model call is asserted, and steps that must not call the model are asserted not to), the reminder cron is kicked explicitly, and the group reminder is captured at the webhook gateway's `/internal/deliver` boundary with its exact payload.

Nine steps, all pinned against develop's route source and repositories:
1. first Blooio DM → auto-account + scripted reply (exactly 1 model call, no `groupDelivery`)
2. `/group` → `group_claim_issued`, 8-char code, copy verbatim, no model call
3. `Eliza link CODE` → `group_bound`, owner-controls copy verbatim, `groupDelivery {kind:"binding", authority v1}`, stored row active / mention_only / owner phone / no lease
4. `@eliza` mention → reply under the owner's personal agent, authority v1
5. ambient under mention_only → `{code:"group_silent", reply:""}` exactly, no model call, no egress
6. owner `Eliza ambient on` → `group_policy_updated` copy, authority **v2** (policy bump), then an ambient reply at v2
7. owner `Eliza remind us in 2 minutes: pizza time` → ack (scripted `inMinutes: 0.05` keeps the cron lane fast), persisted task `metadata.delivery = {platform:"blooio", kind:"group", connectorAccountId, chatId, ownerLabel, authority v2}`; cron fires once into `/internal/deliver` with `X-Internal-Secret` and body `{platform, project, chatId, text:"Reminder for this group from the group owner: pizza time", idempotencyKey}`; receipt row recorded, lease released, authority unchanged; a further sweep fires nothing
8. non-owner `Eliza ambient off` → `group_owner_required`
9. owner `Eliza leave` → `group_binding_revoked` `{kind:"control"}`, authority v3; later mention → `group_binding_suspended`; later ambient → silent. Final: 5 model calls, 1 delivery.

A deliberate mutation (expecting authority v1 instead of v2 at step 6) fails at the real route with `Received version: 2` — the new lease/authority pins are load-bearing.

Harness seam, documented in the spec header: the e2e stack's fresh-DB migrate lane pauses at the 0282 release barrier, so the group tables (0297, 0303, 0304) do not exist in a fresh e2e database; `ensureGroupSchema` applies those three migrations' DDL in order, each skipped when its final object already exists, and asserts all-or-nothing on the first pass and `[]` on the second. #25306 makes fresh ledgers apply the whole journal, after which the seam is a no-op and can be deleted.

## What kind of change is this?

Tests (non-breaking).

# Documentation changes needed?

My changes do not require a change to the project documentation; the spec header documents the protocol, the seam, and the `OPENROUTER_BASE_URL` precondition (the sync script only forwards known keys, so the key must exist in `packages/cloud/shared/.env[.local]` — the spec fails fast with that message otherwise).

## Summary

Adds a dedicated unit suite for `packages/core/src/services/relationships.ts`, which had no same-named test file anywhere in the repository. The diff is one new test file, purely additive (+1098/−0); it does not modify, rewrite, or delete any existing suite and changes no production behavior.

The existing partial suites (`relationships.safe-sort.test.ts`, `relationships-safe-nan.test.ts`, `relationships-analytics-cache.test.ts`, `relationships-pair-predicate.test.ts`, `relationships-conversation-windows.test.ts`, `relationships-verified-members.test.ts`, `relationships-graph-*.test.ts`) already cover comparator ordering, analytics caching, pagination, and the graph builder. This suite covers the untouched remainder of the module's exported surface:

- `calculateRelationshipStrength`: zero-signal floor, interaction-score cap (40), shared-window cap (16), every recency bucket (<1d/7d/30d/90d/older/none), the relationship-type bonus table including the unrecognized-type fallback, clamping to 100, and half-point rounding.
- `countSharedConversationWindows`: empty/single-input floors, third-party filtering, strict-gap window splitting vs exact-boundary gaps staying joined, disjoint windows and rooms counted independently, the `__shared__` bucket for non-string room ids, and custom window sizes.
- Contact lifecycle through a real `RelationshipsService`: default contact shape on `addContact`, persisted `contact_info` component + lifecycle event emission, cache reload through `queryEntities` during `initialize()`, update-merge semantics with immutable `entityId`, removal of present/missing contacts, default categories on initialize and cache teardown on `stop()`, duplicate-category rejection.
- Access control: the full `canAccessContact` privacy matrix (public/private/restricted) with the agent override.
- Search: category OR-membership, tag matching, privacy-level filtering, and searchTerm matching over entity names, custom display names, and entity ids.
- Handles and interactions: platform normalization, case-insensitive duplicate detection returning the stored handle, primary demotion scoped to the same platform, removal results, ordered interaction history with monotonic `lastInteractionAt`, and required-field errors.
- Merging: self-merge and missing-side refusals, deduped handle/tag/category/interaction folding, latest-interaction preservation, secondary goal/threshold fallback, primary-wins custom fields, and secondary-contact removal.
- Goals and follow-ups: goal text trimming/stamping/threshold adoption, all five `cadenceHealth` states under a fixed clock, and the followup threshold chain (contact → goal cadence → default) including never-contacted infinity entries plus archived/blocked exclusion.
- Platform import: seed creation (entity, contact, primary handle, notes/displayName/tags), repeat-import linking, blank-identifier skipping, blank-platform rejection.
- Identity clusters: confirmed-link clustering vs pending-status/wrong-tag/unmetadataed non-links, contact-bearing member preference when resolving a primary, lexicographic fallback, singleton identity, and the `EntityLifecycleEvent` values.

Tests drive the real service and pure functions directly against a hand-built in-memory runtime stub (component/entity stores, recorded events, scripted relationship rows). Assertions are behavioral — observed outputs of the real module — not mock round-trips. One observed quirk is asserted as-is rather than "fixed" in the test: `getRuntimeDb()` throws if `runtime.adapter` is absent, so the stub always carries an `adapter` field.

## Summary

Adds a new unit suite for `packages/ui/src/api/auth-client.ts`, which had no same-named test file anywhere on `develop`. Test-only change — no production code is touched; the diff is one new file, +N/-0.

The suite drives the real module and asserts the discriminated-union mapping each endpoint caller performs from controlled boundary responses (real `Response` objects), not mock echoes:

- **authSetup** — success payload passthrough (URL/method/headers/body asserted), transport errors (`Error` message vs generic "Network error" for non-Error rejections), 409 `already_initialized`, 429 `rate_limited`, 400 `weak_password`, any other 400 → `invalid_display_name` (including an unparseable JSON body via the `.catch(() => ({}))` fallback), unexpected statuses → `server_error` with the status embedded.
- **authLoginPassword** — success passthrough including `rememberDevice` serialization, 429, 401 and 400 both mapped to `invalid_credentials`, other statuses → `server_error`.
- **authLogout** — resolves `{ ok: true }` on success and still resolves `{ ok: true }` when the transport fails (best-effort contract).
- **authMe** over plain HTTP/desktop boundaries — bridge snapshot success with access passthrough, default access synthesis when omitted, unauthorized-reason mapping (`remote_password_not_configured` exact; unknown reasons collapse to `server_error`), empty-snapshot fall-through to HTTP, RPC failure fall-through to HTTP, external-desktop-base short-circuit skipping the bridge, HTTP 401 reason/access propagation, unparseable 401 body degradation to `server_error`, non-401 failures → 503, connection failure → 503.
- **authMe** against a managed shared-agent base — synthetic cloud identity for a stored token with positive or unknown time remaining, `remote_auth_required` with remote access hint when no credential exists, cookie-driven refresh persisting the trimmed token, transient refresh failure surfaced as `503 cloud_unavailable` without clearing stored state, expired-token refresh success/failure paths (failure clears stored state and reports `remote_auth_required`), native owner API key authenticating without a token and suppressing refresh for an expired one.
- **authListSessions** — empty and populated list passthrough, transport failure → 401, 503 preserved, other statuses collapsed to 401.
- **authRevokeSession** — percent-encoded session id in the revoke URL, `{ ok: true }` on success, 404/401 preserved, other endpoint statuses and transport failures collapsed to 500.
- **authChangePassword** — request shape asserted, weak-password mapping, 400 with any other reason degrading to a 500-shaped `server_error`, 401 `invalid_credentials`, 404 `owner_not_found`, 429 `rate_limited`, unexpected statuses with embedded status, non-Error transport rejection → "Network error".

One behavior is asserted exactly as observed in the current implementation rather than as ideally designed: a 400 login response yields `reason: "invalid_credentials"` but coerces `status` to 500 (`res.status === 401 ? 401 : 500`). If that coercion is unintended it deserves its own production fix; this suite records what the code does today.

# test(core): cover followUp service surface

## What

Adds `packages/core/src/services/followUp.test.ts`, a new unit suite for `FollowUpService` (+1018/-0; test-only, no production changes).

`packages/core/src/services/follow-up.test.ts` on develop already covers the teardown/parking lifecycle races through the real TaskService tick loop. This suite is complementary and does not touch that file: it drives the service API directly against deterministic in-memory collaborator doubles (fake runtime + relationships double), asserting observed behavior of the real module.

## Coverage

- `scheduleFollowUp`: unknown-contact rejection (nothing created), full task shape (name, description, tag order `["follow-up", priority, "relationships", "queue"]`, `dueAt`, metadata incl. status/scheduledAt), contact `customFields` mirroring with pre-existing fields preserved, default priority `medium`
- `scheduleMultipleFollowUps`: input-order persistence, per-entry priorities honored, default priority filled
- `getUpcomingFollowUps`: empty queue, ascending sort by scheduled time with stable insertion order for tied timestamps, `includeOverdue=false` drops overdue rows, inclusive day-horizon edges (`now` and exactly `now+days` included, one ms beyond excluded), non-pending statuses excluded, rows whose target contact vanished skipped, missing or unparseable `scheduledAt` treated as epoch-zero overdue rows (included by default, dropped when overdue excluded)
- `completeFollowUp`: unknown-id rejection, storage-failure propagation, atomic completion (queue tag dropped, `status: completed`, `completionNotes`, `completedAt`, contact mirror keys removed while unrelated fields kept), concurrent-completion fallback that unqueues via `updateTask`, refused-transition failures for still-pending (`could not be completed atomically`) and executing (`is already executing`) rows
- `snoozeFollowUp`: `dueAt` shift, `scheduledAt`/`snoozedAt` stamps, `originalScheduledAt` recorded with `createdAt` fallback when no prior `scheduledAt` exists, contact `nextFollowUpAt` updated without clobbering other fields, unknown-id rejection
- `getFollowUpSuggestions`: strict >14-days-since-contact attention filter, candidates with vanished entity records skipped, candidates without relationship analytics skipped, nameless entities labeled `Unknown`, category-specific reason/message selection (family / strong friend / long-neglected colleague / vip / default), ranking by strength-weighted staleness descending
- `follow_up` worker gates and execution: `shouldRun` accepts pending rows with resolvable targets and refuses completed rows, rows without `targetEntityId`, unresolved targets, and anything once the service is stopping; `stop()` swaps the registered worker for the parked never-fire worker and stays idempotent across repeated stops; `execute` writes a reminder memory into the `reminders` table, emits `follow_up:due` with the exact payload contract, transitions the row out of the queue, substitutes default message/reason/priority, returns `{ preserveTask: true }` when the durable claim loses the race, and does not preserve rows whose entity vanished before the claim

## Summary

Adds a dedicated unit suite for `packages/core/src/integrations/managed-provider/http-client.ts`, which had no same-named test file anywhere in the repository. The module was previously exercised only indirectly through the adapter-level `managed-provider.test.ts`; this PR gives the bounded HTTP transport itself first-class behavioral coverage. Test-only change: **one new file, +966/−0**, no production code touched.

## What the suite covers

All requests run through the module's own `testTransport` seam against an in-memory fetch — no network, no DNS; `Date.now` is stubbed only for HTTP-date `Retry-After` parsing.

- **Constructor policy:** managed connections cannot smuggle credentials; private-network mode requires an injected fetch impl; plaintext http origins rejected unless private testing is enabled; loopback/internal hostnames blocked (`ENDPOINT_BLOCKED`) on the public path; connection-id header token grammar and case-insensitive `Authorization` overlap rejection; timeout bounds (100 and 60,000 accepted; 99 / fractional / 60,001 rejected); response byte limits ([1, 5 MiB] integer window — values between the default 1 MiB and the 5 MiB max are valid); exported ceiling constants pinned.
- **`url()` origin pinning:** relative join onto the connection origin, query/fragment preservation, dot-segment normalization that stays on-origin, absolute-URL escape and protocol-relative userinfo rejected (`ENDPOINT_BLOCKED`).
- **Auth-header ownership:** caller `Authorization` is replaced by the local credential's bearer value, stripped entirely when no credential exists, never emitted in managed mode; connection-id header always tagged (default and custom names); POST bodies forwarded untouched.
- **Upstream classification:** plain 401 → `AUTH_EXPIRED`; `credential_revoked` marker upgrades 401 *and* 403 → `AUTH_REVOKED`; plain 403 → `PROVIDER_REJECTED` (recorded observed behavior of the classification order); 429 → `RATE_LIMITED` with numeric, fractional (rounded), HTTP-date (clock-stubbed), stale-date-clamped-to-zero, and unparseable `Retry-After` variants; 5xx → `PROVIDER_FAILURE`.
- **404 semantics:** designed-null default via `requestOptionalJson`, `PROVIDER_REJECTED` via `requestJson` and via explicit `{ notFoundIsNull: false }`.
- **Body bounds & decode:** declared-content-length rejection before reading; default 1 MiB ceiling proven against the exported constant; mid-stream cancellation observed once accumulated bytes exceed the limit (lazy pull-based stream so the underlying source `cancel()` genuinely runs); exact-limit acceptance; fatal UTF-8 → `MALFORMED_RESPONSE`; truncated JSON, empty success body, JSON-null through required vs optional surfaces; schema drift keeps its parse cause.
- **Transport failure mapping:** generic socket failure → `PROVIDER_NETWORK`; `SsrfBlockedError` → `ENDPOINT_BLOCKED` with cause preserved; zero-hop redirect budget refusal; `AbortError`-named failures and an elapsed deadline → `PROVIDER_TIMEOUT`; loopback fakes reachable under `allowPrivateNetworkForTests`.

## What does this PR do?

Covered behaviour, as observed in the live module:

- `getSessionCookieName` → `eliza_session`
- `isDevEnvironment` true for `development` / `dev` (trim + case fold); false for `production`, `test`, blank, unset
- `getCompatApiToken` null when unset; returns `ELIZA_API_TOKEN`; strips a configured `Bearer ` prefix
- `readCookie`: missing/empty header, parts without `=`, empty value, first match on a repeated name, sibling cookies, absent name, percent-decode success and malformed `%ZZ`, array cookie header
- re-exported `extractHeaderValue` / `tokenMatches` / `getProvidedApiToken` (Bearer vs `x-eliza-token` vs `x-api-key`, non-Bearer Authorization fallthrough)
- `roleForIdentityKind`: owner→OWNER, machine→USER, null/undefined/`guest`→NONE
- `embedBoundaryRole`: OWNER→OWNER, ADMIN→USER, null→null
- `resolveEmbedPrincipal`: missing secret/bearer, valid token, tampered token
- `ensureAuthSessionOrBootstrap`: cookie wins over bearer; bearer-only bootstrap; empty auth → 401 then overflow 429 after 20 failures (cookie ignored once limited); missing cookie name falls through to bootstrap
- `ensureCompatApiAuthorized`: trusted loopback without a token; remote 401 with no token; matching remote token; 20 mismatches then 429 even with the correct token; per-IP buckets including null address as `unknown`; `_resetAuthRateLimiter` clears overflow
- `ensureCompatSensitiveRouteAuthorized`: tokenless remote is 403; with a configured token it delegates (match 200 / missing 401)
- `resolveAuthorizedRouteRole`: loopback OWNER before store; 20 failed no-store attempts then 429; no-store matching token is OWNER; store-present matching token is **not** OWNER unless `ELIZA_REQUIRE_LOCAL_AUTH=1`; cookie GET skips CSRF; cookie POST without CSRF is 403 `csrf_required`; cookie POST with derived CSRF succeeds; bearer POST skips CSRF; `allowCookieAuth: false` ignores ambient cookie; missing session id → 401; missing identity kind → NONE; embed ADMIN bearer → USER with `principal`
- `ensureCompatApiAuthorizedAsync` true/false wrapping
- `ensureRouteMinRole` / `ensureRouteAuthorized` on loopback and no-store token paths; unauthenticated remote 401

# Risks

**Medium — backend lifecycle concurrency.**

The change is fail-closed: a stopped-restore request can now return `RESTORE_AUTHORITY_CHANGED` if the captured sandbox generation, placement/deletion state, or lifecycle ownership changes, or if an exclusive lifecycle job exists. This can reject a request that previously raced, but it does not create a new permissive path.

Rollback is a normal revert. There is no schema change, migration, deployment, live-data mutation, worker rollout, or feature activation in this PR.

Scope boundary: this slice closes only the pre-admission race. It does not claim durable ownership after the admission transaction commits; that post-admission authority is intentionally left to successor slice S.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

A manual restore of a stopped dedicated agent previously selected and hydrated a backup, then entered generic provisioning from a replica-read sandbox record. An exclusive lifecycle job could be admitted between those steps, allowing both paths to believe they owned the same agent generation.

This PR makes restore admission the first lifecycle action:

- Captures the exact sandbox identity, tenant, stopped-like status, lifecycle owner pair, execution tier, pool/deletion state, and lifecycle revision used to select and hydrate the backup.
- Accepts only `stopped`, `sleeping`, `disconnected`, or `error`. `pending` is deliberately excluded because create/enqueue compensation can delete a pending row by tenant/id.
- Runs the exact compare-and-set in `dbWrite.transaction`, under the canonical per-agent PostgreSQL advisory lock also used by lifecycle enqueue.
- Requires every captured predicate to remain exact, requires both lifecycle owner fields to remain null, rejects shared/unknown tiers, pool/deletion/replacement-cleanup states, failed warm claims, and any committed active exclusive lifecycle job.
- Atomically moves the exact row to `provisioning`; CAS loss returns `RESTORE_AUTHORITY_CHANGED` and does not reuse an already-running record.
- Pins the selected backup ID and performs no replica read, replacement cleanup, database/env/key/provider/billing work before admission.
- Adds a real PostgreSQL `READ COMMITTED` race test: enqueue holds the same advisory lock while a trigger gate pauses before the job insert; restore admission waits, then observes the committed job on its fresh `UPDATE` snapshot and refuses admission.

This is intentionally **R, not S**. After the admission commit, a later enqueue or non-exclusive job can still race external provisioning. In particular, `agent_message` may still see `provisioning` with a null bridge and enter shared bootstrap; snapshot/cleanup/writeback paths also need durable fencing. Slice S must use typed durable authority fields and exact token/locator checks; it must not encode ownership in `error_message`.

Open-PR overlap was rescanned across all 125 open PRs, all authors, immediately before publication. Only #24960, #24961, and #25034 touch one of these five files, all in `eliza-sandbox.ts` and all authored by `byt61`. Their current hunks are unrelated: #24960/#24961 change the billing fallback near line 1463, and #25034 changes surrogate-safe restore-error truncation near line 12101. None overlaps the admission hunks.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking, backend concurrency and fail-closed admission).

## Summary

Adds real unit coverage for `packages/app-core/src/runtime/startup/server-only-host.ts`, the bind-first server-only host that owns API binding, onboarding deferral, runtime publication/restart, sandbox registration, and idempotent shutdown. There is no same-named test file on `develop`. This PR changes no production behaviour.

The suite drives the real `startServerOnlyHost` orchestrator. Socket bind, first-run disk, and Redis are stubbed as I/O seams; assertions observe host sequencing and projected `AppStartupStateMachine` phases, not mock echo.

Recorded behaviour (what the code does):

- Port selection: unset `ELIZA_API_PORT` binds the server-only default `2138`; a set `ELIZA_API_PORT` uses the desktop resolver. A rebound listener is synced into `ELIZA_API_PORT` / `ELIZA_UI_PORT` / `ELIZA_PORT` and CORS ports are invalidated.
- Local-agent IPC (`localAgentMode: true` without `ELIZA_API_EXPOSE_PORT`) initializes the route kernel with `skipListen: true` and does **not** sync a never-bound port. `ELIZA_API_EXPOSE_PORT=1` re-opens TCP listen.
- API bind failure logs `Error.stack` when present, the message when `stack` is missing, or `String(err)` for non-Errors; boot is skipped and the original rejection is rethrown.
- Immediate boot binds first (`initialAgentState: "starting"`), then `runtime-starting` (attempt 1). A still-pending post-ready phase projects `features-starting`. `complete` during boot projects `ready`; `failed` during boot projects `degraded`. Post-ready callbacks before the runtime is published do not emit phases.
- After publish, `complete` → `ready` and `failed` → `degraded`. `pending` from `degraded` throws `Invalid startup transition: degraded -> features-starting` (the real state machine rejects it).
- Initial boot throw: close API, rethrow original, project `failed`/`error`. Initial boot that returns `undefined`: close API, return `undefined`, do **not** invoke `onServerOnlyHostReady`.
- Deferred onboarding: register the boot closure, bind as `not_started`, project `awaiting-onboarding`, do not boot immediately. The registered closure on success updates the runtime; on throw wraps with `Runtime boot after onboarding failed` and keeps the registration; on empty runtime throws `Runtime boot after onboarding returned no runtime` and keeps the registration.
- `onRestart` while deferred funnels into `triggerDeferredRuntimeBoot("agent start requested via API")`. After a live runtime, restart stops with `"server-only restart"`, increments attempt, and returns the new runtime. Restart boot throw rethrows the original (not wrapped) and does not close the API. Restart that yields no runtime returns `null` without closing the API. Restart with no published runtime and clear deferral boots without `stopRuntime`.
- Sandbox: `register()` then `startHeartbeat(30000)`. Register failure logs, calls `runtime.reportError("eliza.sandboxRegistry", err, { phase: "register" })` when a runtime exists, and still starts the heartbeat. Close stops the heartbeat and unregisters; unregister failure warns and still stops the runtime.
- `close` is idempotent: API and runtime stop once. A host that never published a runtime calls `stopWithoutRuntime`.

## What does this PR do?

Adds `packages/agent/src/api/agent-admin-routes.test.ts`, which imports
`handleAgentAdminRoutes` from `./agent-admin-routes` (the same relative path
production uses) and drives the real handler.

I/O seams (config load/save, path resolution, host vault, first-run wipe, model
label, runtime quiesce) are isolated so the suite does not touch a live PGlite
directory or vault. The system under test is never replaced with a mock: the
suite asserts HTTP status, reported agent state, PGlite delete guards, and vault
key names against the real module.

Covered branches:

1. Unmatched method/path returns `false` without writing a response (including
   `POST /api/agent/start`, which is owned by the lifecycle module).
2. Restart: 501 with no handler, 409 while `agentState === "restarting"`,
   successful swap (quiesce previous runtime, clear chat connection, report
   `running`, fire optional swap/activation callbacks), fallback agent names
   (`character.name` → `ui.assistant.name` → `agents.list[0].name` → default
   style preset; a whitespace-only assistant name does **not** fall through
   `??` to the list), null/Error/non-Error `onRestart` restores the previous
   reported state.
3. Reset: `runtime.stop({ fast: true })`, skip stop when runtime is null,
   env/config/default PGlite path selection, refuse delete unless basename is
   `.elizadb`, skip delete when the path does not exist, first-run wipe +
   persist, wipe of `ELIZAOS_CLOUD_API_KEY` / `ELIZAOS_CLOUD_BASE_URL` /
   `ELIZAOS_CLOUD_ENABLED`, per-key vault miss is ignored, vault-open failure
   warns and still returns `{ ok: true }`, conversation map clear, 500 when
   `stop` or `loadElizaConfig` throws.

Adds colocated unit tests for `packages/agent/src/config/zod-schema.ts`, which previously had no same-named test file. The module exports `CharacterSchema` and `ElizaSchema`. This PR changes no production behaviour.

The suite drives the real Zod validators (no mocks):

- **CharacterSchema**: empty overlay, fully populated round-trip, strict unknown-key rejection, name/username length caps, bio string-or-array (including empty queues), system overflow, adjective/topic empty-item and overflow, style clear-form, messageExamples empty group vs single group vs extra keys, postExamples empty queue.
- **ElizaSchema**: optional empty root; `CommandsSchema` defaults (`native`/`nativeSkills` = `"auto"`) applied when omitted; agents list empty/single/multi plus missing-id rejection.
- **Broadcast `superRefine`**: skip when `agents.list` is missing or empty; skip when broadcast is omitted; strategy-only objects; empty peer queue; single known id; mixed known/unknown ids with the documented `Unknown agent id "…" (not in agents.list).` message and `["broadcast", peer, idx]` paths; invalid strategy and non-array catchall.
- **Bindings, approvals, connectors/streaming passthrough vs strict defaults, memory QMD numeric bounds, env catchall, browser profile name regex + `cdpPort`/`cdpUrl` refine, gateway/web/discovery unions, auth/logging/diagnostics/embedding, remaining nested objects** (deployment, linked accounts, routing, ui, roles, cron, talk, skills, plugins).

6a:Tbbe,# Overall Project Summary: Aug 23, 2026

Development on August 23 focused on hardening system stability and data integrity, with significant efforts directed toward deterministic sorting, Unicode safety, and expanded unit test coverage. The team also made progress on cloud infrastructure, including voice runtime optimizations and the bootstrapping of a journal-backed production controller for synthetic worlds.

## ✅ Completed Work

### System Stability and Data Integrity
*   **Deterministic Sorting:** Implemented `Number.isFinite` guards across `core`, `agent`, and plugins to eliminate non-deterministic sorting caused by `NaN` values ([elizaos/eliza#25970](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/25970), [elizaos/eliza#25949](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/25949), [elizaos/eliza#25931](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/25931), [elizaos/eliza#25913](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/25913)).
*   **Input Validation:** Enforced strict canonical integer parsing to reject whitespace-padded inputs ([elizaos/eliza#25843](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/25843)).

### Unicode and String Safety
*   **Standardized Truncation:** Implemented `truncateWellFormed` and `toWellFormedUnicode` across services to prevent malformed Unicode and lone surrogate pairs in logs and UI previews ([elizaos/eliza#25922](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/25922), [elizaos/eliza#25915](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/25915), [elizaos/eliza#25844](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/25844)).

### Cloud and Agent Infrastructure
*   **Performance & Reliability:** Improved cloud stability via durable sandbox replacement ([elizaos/eliza#25721](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/25721)) and reduced voice runtime latency through improved warmups ([elizaos/eliza#26657](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/26657)).
*   **Synthetic World Controller:** Bootstrapped the production controller using a journal-backed approach ([elizaos/eliza#25407](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/25407)).

### Testing Expansion
*   **Test Coverage:** Massively expanded unit test coverage by adding colocated Vitest suites across `agent`, `core`, `cloud`, and `app-core` packages ([elizaos/eliza#26265](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/26265), [elizaos/eliza#26264](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/26264), [elizaos/eliza#26263](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/26263)).

Exact just-in-time confirmation remains required at the moment any protected provider, identity, database, workflow, deployment, or lifecycle action would occur.75:T1977,## Summary
The route-level model downloader `downloadModel` in `plugins/plugin-local-inference/src/local-inference-routes.ts` resumes an interrupted download by sending a `Range: bytes=<n>-` header and then opening the staging file in append mode whenever a `.part` file exists (`flags: existingPartial > 0 ? "a" : "w"`). It never verifies the server actually honored the range (HTTP 206). If the origin ignores Range and replies HTTP 200 with the full body — common for CDN redirect targets, gated/proxy repos, or mirrors — the full file is appended onto the stale partial bytes, producing a corrupt GGUF. `record.total` is also miscomputed as `existingPartial + fullSize`. The corruption passes the only integrity check (`isGgufFile` reads just the first 4 bytes, which are still "GGUF" from the old partial), and there is no sha256 verification against an expected hash, so the corrupt file is renamed to final, registered as an installed model, and auto-assigned to the TEXT_SMALL/TEXT_LARGE/TEXT_EMBEDDING slots via `ensureDefaultAssignment`. The sibling canonical `services/downloader.ts` in the same package already guards this exact case (`if (startByte > 0 && response.statusCode !== 206) { startByte = 0; received = 0 }` then `flags: startByte > 0 ? "a" : "w"`); the route-level copy diverged and dropped the guard.

## Reproduction
```
Ran a local Vitest probe in plugins/plugin-local-inference (real fs + real local HTTP origin; only ELIZA_STATE_DIR and ELIZA_HF_BASE_URL redirected). Steps: (1) set ELIZA_HF_BASE_URL to a local http server that IGNORES Range and always answers `200` with the full body `GGUF`+`REAL-MODEL-BODY` (19 bytes); (2) seed a stale partial `<state>/local-inference/downloads/eliza-1-2b.part` = `GGUF`+`STALE-PARTIAL`; (3) call the exported `applyLocalInferenceManagementMutation({ op: "start_download", modelId: "eliza-1-2b" })`, which runs `startDownload` -> `downloadModel`; (4) poll for the final file `<state>/local-inference/models/eliza-1-2b.gguf`.
Observed output: `stored length: 36 expected: 19` and `stored bytes: "GGUFSTALE-PARTIALGGUFREAL-MODEL-BODY"`. Expected: exactly `GGUFREAL-MODEL-BODY` (19 bytes). The corrupt file was renamed to final and written into registry.json as an installed model. Test asserted `stored.equals(FULL)` -> failed (false). Command: `npx vitest run src/__probe_resume.test.ts`.
```

## Proposed fix
Mirror the sibling downloader's guard in `downloadModel`: after receiving the response and validating 2xx, compute `let effectiveStart = existingPartial; if (existingPartial > 0 && response.statusCode !== 206) { effectiveStart = 0; record.received = 0; }`, then use `effectiveStart` for both `record.total = effectiveStart + contentLength` and `flags: effectiveStart > 0 ? "a" : "w"`. Bounded to ~6 lines in one function; no signature/API change. Test plan (>=10 lines, honest): a Vitest suite standing up two local http origins — one that honors Range (206 + remaining bytes) and one that ignores it (200 + full body) — seeding a stale `.part`, driving `applyLocalInferenceManagementMutation({op:"start_download"})`, and asserting the final `models/<id>.gguf` bytes exactly equal the full file in BOTH cases (correct resume for 206, clean restart for 200); plus a regression assertion that `record.total`/registry size match the true file length. The probe already written proves the failing case and converts directly into the 200-path test.

## Evidence plan
The PR will attach: the failing-before / passing-after Vitest output for both the 200 (ignore-range) and 206 (honor-range) origins; a hexdump/length comparison of the stored `models/<id>.gguf` showing 19 bytes (correct) vs the current 36-byte `GGUFSTALE-PARTIALGGUFREAL-MODEL-BODY` corruption; and a diff showing the route-level guard now matches services/downloader.ts (statusCode !== 206 -> restart from 0).
